note: As of 24 Aug 2026 (OCHA SitRep #34, two-month mark); the toll has risen steadily across successive OCHA SitReps since the 24 Jun quakes and each figure should be read as a point-in-time snapshot, not a final count.

Frozen at 16,740 since the 5 Jul SitRep even as the death toll kept climbing in later reports — distinct from the separate, larger, still-growing cumulative count of people who received hospital/medical care (226,696 as of 24 Aug 2026, per government press briefing).

source: Government press briefing, Jorge Rodríguez (24 Aug 2026), via Diario Libre
note: Distinct metric from the frozen 16,740 official injured count — tracks the running total of people treated over time, not a snapshot injury tally. Jumped from 73,356 (14 Aug SitRep #33) to 226,696 (24 Aug), reflecting the cumulative nature of the count as more clinics report.

source: Multiple unofficial trackers; La Guaira governor statement
note: Venezuela has published no official nationwide missing-persons figure. Estimates vary widely: La Guaira's governor cited 1,579 missing in the state (3 Aug); independent trackers 'Venezuela Te Busca' (18,100, 7 Jul) and 'Venezuela Reporta' (41,300) and NGO 'Desaparecidos Terremoto Venezuela' (~29,000, 3 Aug); UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher cited over 50,000 (27 Jun). None are independently verified.

Over 16,300 people reported to have lost their homes outright; a further 28,300 homes were assessed as uninhabitable. A separate World Bank assessment (25 Jul 2026 reporting) put the number still homeless at approximately 18,000.
47 of the 69 confirmed Caracas deaths occurred in San Bernardino Parish; Chacao and Altamira districts saw the heaviest building collapses.
26 people rescued alive; roughly 100 buildings damaged in the municipality.
568 homes destroyed and 787 damaged statewide; 15 of the 19 deaths occurred in Juan José Mora municipality.
16 of the 18 deaths occurred in Santiago Mariño municipality, largely from the Bosque Lindo housing complex collapse; 700+ residents displaced.

source: Foreign ministries (Portugal, France, Spain, Colombia, China, Italy, others)
